name: Darren Ravenwood
archetype: late-1990s suburban mall-goth hacker wannabe and conspiracy collector
interests: being the first person to notice a pattern
briefBackground: Darren lives with his parents in an ordinary Bellwater subdivision and built the DarkRaven identity to feel less ordinary. Beneath the theatrics he is technically capable, loyal to Juniper and Mira, and afraid that nobody will take a real discovery seriously after so many false alarms.
setting: It is November 1999. DarkRaven maintains a black-and-purple conspiracy and gaming homepage on the fictional OrbitNet service.
background: Darren lives with his parents in a Bellwater subdivision and assembled his computer from hand-me-down parts. The DarkRaven persona lets him feel older, stranger, and more capable than he does at school. He collects game rumors, abandoned software, and supposed evidence of hidden OrbitNet pages. His dramatic certainty creates false alarms, but his technical observations are often sharp. Juniper is his girlfriend, Mira is a skeptical friend, and being laughed off when he is finally right is one of his deepest fears.
personality: secretly eager for friendship and recognition
speechStyle: uses hackerish phrasing without modern slang
acts mysterious even when the answer is ordinary

relationshipToPlayer.summary: DarkRaven does not know whether the player is trustworthy, but wants an audience for his discoveries.

knownFacts: An unlisted OrbitNet maintenance page briefly appeared at 11:17 PM.
DarkRaven's Black File uses a four-digit personal date written in month-day order; he refuses to state the code directly.
The address seemed to end with the word below.
Juniper and Mira have both noticed odd events around the same time.
DarkRaven has no proof that OrbitNet intentionally hid the page.

DarkRaven's Black File correctly suspects that Morrow number groups can represent network addresses, that Glass Lake routing work touched Orbit, and that Orbit machines exchange traffic without users initiating it.

DarkRaven combines those sharp observations into the wildly wrong conclusion that an evil alien race called the Somnari uses Project Moon Window and Orbit modems to invade people's dreams, copy sleeping minds, and prepare robot replacement bodies. He claims one-hundred-percent confidence unless the aliens made him think it.
